  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors

          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"

      required:

      properties:
        firstName:

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept,
            otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is
            dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped. The result must be '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits, and this
            E.164 value is stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be
            a syntactically valid address; the value is stored and returned
            lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-

          type: string
          format: date

## Summary

I implemented the `customerCode` assignment rule (`<LAST3>-<NNNN>`) with each piece of logic in its proper place:

**New logic — one small, single-responsibility unit**
- `rest/validation/CustomerCodeGenerator.java` — a pure formatter that builds the code from a last name and the current owner count (`LAST3` = upper-cased first three letters; `NNNN` = zero-padded `count + 1`). This mirrors the existing `TelephoneNormalizer`/`EmailNormalizer` style.

**Wiring it into the create flow (mirrors existing normalization there)**
- `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` now assigns the code just before saving, sourcing the count from the service. It runs only on create, so `updateOwner` never rewrites it.

**Counting owners (reused down the existing layers)**
- `OwnerRepository.count()` added to the interface, implemented in the JPA and JDBC impls; the Spring Data repository (the profile the tests use) gets it for free as a standard derived method.
- `ClinicService.countOwners()` delegates to the repository, consistent with the facade's other methods.

**Persistence & exposure of the field**
- `Owner` entity: added the `customerCode` field mapped to a new `customer_code` column, with getter/setter.
- `openapi.yml`: added `customerCode` as a `readOnly` property on the `Owner` schema, so the generated DTO carries it and MapStruct maps it by name into `GET` responses automatically.
- Added the `customer_code` column to all four DB schemas (hsqldb, h2, postgres, mysql); it's nullable so the existing seed data still loads.

The acceptance test's key checks hold: codes are prefixed `SMI-`/`JON-`, and because the count is read immediately before each insert (auto-flushed within the transaction), the second owner's sequence is exactly one greater than the first.
